facts.statement: Fossils of Pholidosaurus have been found in northwestern Germany.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in northwestern Germany.

facts.statement: Pholidosaurus lived during the Berriasian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The genus is known to have existed during the Berriasian-Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Pholidosaurus was similar in appearance and about the same size as the modern gharial.
facts.quote: It is similar in appearance to and about as large as the modern gharial.

facts.statement: The type species, P. schaumburgensis, was named in 1841 from fossils found in the Wealden of Bückeburg, Germany.
facts.quote: The type species of Pholidosaurus is P. schaumburgensis, named in 1841 from the Wealden of Bückeburg, Germany.

facts.statement: The individual represented by the type mold was estimated to be around 25 cm in length.
facts.quote: The individual that the mould belonged to is thought to have been around 25 cm in length.

facts.statement: The genus Macrorhynchus is considered a junior synonym of Pholidosaurus.
facts.quote: Macrorhynchus is a junior synonym of Pholidosaurus.

facts.statement: The species Petrosuchus laevidens was originally based on fossils collected from Swanage, England.
facts.quote: Petrosuchus laevidens was based on this cranium and a mandibular ramus called BMNH 41099, both of which were collected from Swanage, England.

facts.statement: A 2002 study determined that Steneosaurus purbeckensis is the same species as Pholidosaurus decipiens, resulting in the combination Pholidosaurus purbeckensis.
facts.quote: However, in 2002, a new study showed that S. purbeckensis was conspecific with P. decipiens, creating the new combination Pholidosaurus purbeckensis.

facts.statement: Smith et al. (2016) suggested that Pholidosaurus purbeckensis is not closely related to the type species but is instead related to Fortignathus and Dyrosauridae.
facts.quote: In an SVPCA abstract, Smith et al. (2016) noted that Pholidosaurus purbeckensis is not congeneric with the type species, and instead is closely related to Fortignathus and members of Dyrosauridae.

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker classified Pholidosaurus in the family Goniopholididae in 1887 based on amphicoelous vertebrae and an orbit communicating with the lateral temporal fossa.
facts.quote: Richard Lydekker assigned Pholidosaurus to the family Goniopholididae in 1887 along with Hylaeochampsa, Theriosuchus, Goniopholis, and Petrosuchus because the vertebrae are amphicoelus and the orbit communicates with the lateral temporal fossa.

facts.statement: Buckley and Brochu (1999) concluded that Pholidosaurus formed a long-snouted clade that was the sister group to Crocodylia.
facts.quote: Buckley and Brochu (1999) concluded that Pholidosaurus, Sokotosuchus, Dyrosauridae, and Thalattosuchia formed a longirostrine clade that was the sister taxon to Crocodylia.

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate that Thalattosuchia is a more basal lineage when dyrosaurids are excluded from the analysis.
facts.quote: More recent studies have revealed Thalattosuchia as a more basal clade when dyrosaurids are removed from the data set.

facts.statement: Pholidosaurus is the type genus of the family Pholidosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pholidosauridae

facts.statement: An early description by Lydekker (1888) noted that the orbit was slightly smaller than the supratemporal fossa, the nasal bone reached the premaxilla, and the vomer appeared on the palate.
facts.quote: Una temprana descripción del género por Lydekker (1888) mencionó que la órbita es levemente menor que la fosa supratemporal, el hueso nasal alcanza al premaxilar, y el vómer aparece en el paladar.

facts.statement: The type species Pholidosaurus schaumburgensis was named in 1841 from the Wealden Group in Bückeburg, Germany.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Pholidosaurus es P. schaumburgensis, nombrada en 1841 del Grupo Wealden, o Arenas de Hastings Sand, de Bückeburg, Alemania.

facts.statement: The species was named based on a natural mold of part of a thorax discovered around 1830 in the Berriasian Obernkirchen Sandstone.
facts.quote: P. schaumburgensis fue nombrado sobre la base de un molde natural de parte de un tórax descubierto hacia 1830 en la Arenisca Obernkirchen del Berriasiano.

facts.statement: The individual that produced the type mold is believed to have been about 25 centimeters long.
facts.quote: El individuo que lo produjo se cree que tenía cerca de 25 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Macrorhynchus is a more modern synonym of Pholidosaurus, named in 1843 from the Wealden in southern England with the type species M. meyeri.
facts.quote: Macrorhynchus es un sinónimo más moderno de Pholidosaurus. Fue nombrado en 1843 del Grupo Wealden en el sur de Inglaterra, siendo su especie tipo M. meyeri.

facts.statement: P. meyeri differs from the type species P. schaumburgensis in that the bony bar separating the supratemporal fenestra is rounded, whereas in the type species it is round.
facts.quote: P. meyeri difiere de P. schaumburgensis en que la barra ósea que separa la fenestra supratemporal es redondeada, mientras que en la especie tipo ésta es redonda.

facts.statement: P. decipiens was used to describe a partial skull, BMNH 28432, originally assigned to the new genus and species Petrosuchus laevidens by Richard Owen in 1878.
facts.quote: P. decipiens se usó para describir un cráneo parcial, BMNH 28432, que fue originalmente asignado al nuevo género y especie Petrosuchus laevidens por Richard Owen en 1878.

facts.statement: BMNH 28432 was reassigned to Pholidosaurus while BMNH 41099 retained the name Petrosuchus laevidens.
facts.quote: BMNH 28432 fue reasignado a Pholidosaurus y BMNH 41099 retuvo el nombre de Petrosuchus laevidens.

facts.statement: The holotype is an almost complete skull named DORCM G97, which lacks the anterior part of the face.
facts.quote: El holotipo es un cráneo casi completo, nombrado como DORCM G97, que carece de la porción anterior del rostro.

facts.statement: The skull was found in Swanage or on the Isle of Purbeck, though the exact locality was not specified by the original author.
facts.quote: El cráneo fue encontrado en Swanage o en la isla de Purbeck (de aquí el nombre de la especie), aunque la localidad exacta de la que proviene el cráneo no fue especificada por el autor de la descripción original.

facts.statement: A 2002 study proposed that S. purbeckensis belonged to P. decipiens.
facts.quote: En 2002 un nuevo estudio propuso que S. purbeckensis pertenecía a P. decipiens.

facts.statement: Because the name S. purbeckensis had priority over P. decipiens but not the genus Pholidosaurus, the name Pholidosaurus purbeckensis is considered to have priority.
facts.quote: Ya que el nombre S. purbeckensis tenía prioridad sobre P. decipiens, pero no así el género Pholidosaurus, se considera que el nombre Pholidosaurus purbeckensis tiene prioridad.

facts.statement: It was considered a more modern synonym of P. purbeckensis by both Salisbury et al. (1999) and Salisbury (2002).
facts.quote: Esta fue considerado como un sinónimo más moderno de P. purbeckensis tanto por Salisbury et al. (1999) como Salisbury (2002).

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker assigned Pholidosaurus to the family Goniopholididae in 1887 along with Hylaeochampsa, Theriosuchus, Goniopholis, and Petrosuchus because their vertebrae are amphicoelous and the orbit communicates with the lateral temporal fossa.
facts.quote: Richard Lydekker asignó Pholidosaurus a la familia Goniopholididae en 1887 junto con Hylaeochampsa, Theriosuchus, Goniopholis y Petrosuchus debido a que sus vértebras son anficelas y la órbita se comunica con la fosa temporal lateral.

facts.statement: Buckley and Brochu (1999) concluded that Pholidosaurus, Sokotosuchus, Dyrosauridae, and Thalattosuchia form a longirostrine clade that was the sister taxon to Crocodylia.
facts.quote: Buckley y Brochu (1999) concluyeron que Pholidosaurus, Sokotosuchus, Dyrosauridae y Thalattosuchia forman un clado longirostrino que era el taxón hermano de Crocodylia.

facts.statement: Pholidosaurus has recently been reassigned to the family Pholidosauridae, along with the genera Elosuchus, Sarcosuchus, and Terminonaris.
facts.quote: Pholidosaurus ha sido recientemente reasignado a la familia Pholidosauridae, junto con los géneros Elosuchus, Sarcosuchus y Terminonaris.

facts.statement: Jouve et al. (2006) concluded that Pholidosaurus was a pholidosaurid, although in their phylogenetic analysis, thalattosuchians were included in the family, which could be considered paraphyletic without them.
facts.quote: Jouve et al. (2006) concluyó que Pholidosaurus era un folidosáurido, aunque en sus análisis filogenético, los talatosuquios fueron incluidos en la familia, la cual podría ser considerada parafilética sin ellos.

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Tithonian to the Aptian, between 149.2 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Aptian (149.2 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Barbini et al. (2026) reported evidence that the endocranial anatomy of P. purbeckensis is more similar to goniopholidids than dyrosaurids and found possible osteological correlates of nasal salt glands.
facts.quote: Barbini et al. (2026) provide new information on the internal cranial anatomy of Pholidosaurus purbeckensis, reporting evidence of greater similarity of the endocranial anatomy to that of goniopholidids than dyrosaurids, and evidence of presence of possible osteological correlates of nasal salt glands.

rejected.statement: Brochu et al. (2002) found that Pholidosaurus and Thalattosuchia formed a clade that was the sister group to a clade containing Sokotosuchus and Dyrosauridae.
rejected.quote: In the study, both taxa formed a clade that was the sister taxon to a clade containing Sokotosuchus and Dyrosauridae.

rejected.statement: The species name P. decipiens refers to Owen's mistake.
rejected.quote: P. decipiens fue llamada así en referencia a la equivocación de Owen.

rejected.statement: P. purbeckensis was originally described as a species of Steneosaurus in 1888.
rejected.quote: P. purbeckensis fue originalmente descrita como una especie de Steneosaurus en 1888.

rejected.quote: P. laevis fue nombrada en 1913, basada en un cráneo parcial conocido como BMNH R3414, procedente de Swanage.
